output.brief: FCR fell because of the 14 April Finance change, not the new starters. It cut the credit an agent can apply on a call from £100 to £25 and automatically refers larger cases to the Billing Resolution team. Referrals of billing calls went from 7% to 54% in the same week FCR dropped. Referred calls resolve first time only about 34% of the time, and non-referred calls are unchanged at 82%. Tenured agents fell as much as the April intake (67% versus 66%), and the tariff mix and the IVR redesign don't fit the timing or the unchanged non-referred results. Complaints rose over the same period, but the link to FCR isn't established. I'm fairly confident, though I haven't tested this by changing the limit. Next steps: don't put the April intake on performance plans, because the site-wide figure isn't their fault. Agree a revised credit limit with Finance and trial it on two teams for six weeks, with post-call sampling of credits. Track FCR, referral rate and unsupported credits. Ask MI for agent-level and team-level breakdowns, which take about a day. Hold off on rebuilding the dashboard and on a centre-wide change until the trial reports.
